proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a finite-menu identification boundary with smooth positive complete-law twins, infinite-support whole-law identification, and a constructive bounded-rate upper certificate. The D0.5 math panel passed, but the general reviewer graded the delivered package subfield below the required field floor. A matching full-experiment lower modulus, sharp design dependence, and a demonstrated gain from cause labels remain open; formalization was not started.
tldr: A finite randomized menu of strictly positive competing-hazard switches identifies causal net risk exactly only at the positive intersections obtained by extending an observed post-switch exposure line to the elimination axis; smooth positive complete-law twins separate every other time. Infinite active timing support identifies the whole frailty law. Stability has a qualitative elbow: without common rate bounds there is no uniform consistency, whereas on a fixed common rate rectangle an explicit interpolation procedure gives a full-experiment modulus upper bound \(\delta^{1-o(1)}\) and an honest fixed-confidence radius \(n_j^{-1/2+o(1)}\). This is a constructive upper result, and the matching fixed-rectangle lower modulus remains open.
gap: The duration literature identifies dependent competing frailties from open regressor variation, structured treatment effects from stochastic treatment-initiation timing, and scalar frailty models from minimal time variation, but it does not state the exact elimination-risk boundary created by a finite randomized competing-hazard switch menu or quantify its stability.
fill: The paper pairs analytic continuation for sufficiency with squared line-vanishing smooth perturbations for necessity, proves whole-law identification in an explicit infinite-menu experiment for every infinite allocation support, and connects the resulting uniqueness claims to adjoint-range and restricted-modulus inference.
